claim: When Evaluation Periods and Datapoints to Alarm are set to different values, you are setting an M out of N alarm.
q: What is an M out of N CloudWatch alarm?
ev: When you configure **Evaluation Periods** and **Datapoints to Alarm** as different values, you're setting an "M out of N" alarm.

claim: For alarms on Amazon EC2 metrics that stop, terminate, reboot or recover an instance, AWS recommends treating missing data as missing and triggering only when the alarm is in the ALARM state; metric reporting can be interrupted even when the instance is healthy.
q: How should an EC2 alarm that stops or recovers an instance treat missing data?
v: trigger only when in the ALARM state
ev: This is rare, but can happen when the metric reporting is interrupted, even when the Amazon EC2 instance is healthy. For alarms on Amazon EC2 metrics that are configured to take stop, terminate, reboot, or recover actions, we recommend that you configure those alarms to treat missing data as `missing`, and to have these alarms trigger only when in the ALARM state.

claim: Except for Auto Scaling actions, alarm actions happen only on state transitions and are not performed again if the condition persists for hours or days.
q: Does a CloudWatch alarm repeat its action while it stays in the ALARM state?
v: not performed again if the condition persists
cond: Auto Scaling actions are the exception.
ev: Except for Auto Scaling actions, the actions happen only on state transitions, and are not performed again if the condition persists for hours or days.

claim: A CloudWatch alarm can notify an Amazon SNS topic, invoke a Lambda function, perform EC2 actions (stop, terminate, reboot, recover) when it is based on EC2 metrics, scale an Auto Scaling group, and create Systems Manager OpsItems or Incident Manager incidents.
q: Which actions can a CloudWatch alarm take?
v: Notify one or more subscribers by using an Amazon Simple Notification Service topic
stopping, terminating, rebooting, or recovering an EC2 instance
ev: Notify one or more subscribers by using an Amazon Simple Notification Service topic. Subscribers can be applications as well as persons.
Invoke a Lambda function. This is the easiest way for you to automate custom actions on alarm state changes.
Alarms based on EC2 metrics can also perform EC2 actions, such as stopping, terminating, rebooting, or recovering an EC2 instance.
Alarms can perform actions to scale an Auto Scaling group.
Alarms can create OpsItems in Systems Manager Ops Center or create incidents in AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager. These actions are performed only when the alarm goes into ALARM state.

claim: Alarms emit events to Amazon EventBridge when they change state, and you can set up EventBridge to trigger other actions for these state changes.
q: How can an alarm state change trigger actions beyond the alarm's own action list?
v: emit events to Amazon EventBridge when they change state
trigger other actions for these state changes
ev: Alarms also emit events to Amazon EventBridge when they change state, and you can set up Amazon EventBridge to trigger other actions for these state changes.

claim: You can add the stop, terminate or reboot action to an alarm on an EC2 per-instance metric (including basic and detailed monitoring metrics in the AWS/EC2 namespace, and custom metrics with the InstanceId dimension) as long as the InstanceId value refers to a valid running EC2 instance.
q: On which metrics can a CloudWatch alarm stop, terminate or reboot an EC2 instance?
sc: alarms with EC2 stop, terminate or reboot actions
ev: You can add the stop, terminate, or reboot, actions to any alarm that is set on an Amazon EC2 per-instance metric, including basic and detailed monitoring metrics provided by Amazon CloudWatch (in the AWS/EC2 namespace), in addition to any custom metrics that include the "InstanceId=" dimension, as long as the InstanceId value refers to a valid running Amazon EC2 instance.

claim: The EC2 recover alarm action can be used only with the StatusCheckFailed_System metric, not with StatusCheckFailed_Instance.
q: Which EC2 status check metric can trigger the recover alarm action?
sc: alarms with the EC2 recover action
n: The same page earlier says the recover action can be added to alarms on any EC2 per-instance metric except StatusCheckFailed_Instance. This fact uses the sentence in the recover section.
ev: The recover action can be used only with `StatusCheckFailed_System`, not with `StatusCheckFailed_Instance`.

claim: A recovered EC2 instance is identical to the original, including the instance ID, private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses and all instance metadata; terminated instances cannot be recovered.
q: What stays the same after a CloudWatch alarm recovers an EC2 instance?
ev: Terminated instances cannot be recovered. A recovered instance is identical to the original instance, including the instance ID, private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses, and all instance metadata.

claim: During EC2 instance recovery the instance is migrated during an instance reboot, and any data that is in memory is lost.
q: Is in-memory data kept when a CloudWatch alarm recovers an EC2 instance?
v: any data that is in-memory is lost
ev: During instance recovery, the instance is migrated during an instance reboot, and any data that is in-memory is lost.

claim: The reboot alarm action is recommended for Instance Health Check failures, while the recover alarm action is suited for System Health Check failures.
q: Which alarm action fits an EC2 instance status check failure and which fits a system status check failure?
v: recommended for Instance Health Check failures
suited for System Health Check failures
sc: alarms with EC2 reboot or recover actions
ev: The reboot alarm action is recommended for Instance Health Check failures (as opposed to the recover alarm action, which is suited for System Health Check failures).

claim: A recover alarm automatically recovers an EC2 instance that becomes impaired due to an underlying hardware failure or a problem that requires AWS involvement to repair; the recover action is supported only on some instance types.
q: When does a CloudWatch alarm recover an EC2 instance, and does it work for every instance type?
v: supported only on some instance types
sc: alarms with the EC2 recover action
ev: You can create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors an Amazon EC2 instance and automatically recovers the instance if it becomes impaired due to an underlying hardware failure or a problem that requires AWS involvement to repair.
The recover action is supported only on some instance types.

claim: With the stop alarm action you can easily restart the instance later and keep the same instance ID and root volume; a terminated instance cannot be restarted and you must launch a new instance.
q: What is the difference between the stop and terminate alarm actions for EC2?
sc: alarms with EC2 stop or terminate actions
ev: The main difference between using the stop and the terminate alarm actions is that you can easily restart a stopped instance if you need to run it again later. You can also keep the same instance ID and root volume. However, you cannot restart a terminated instance. Instead, you must launch a new instance.

claim: EC2 instances with an EBS volume as the root device can be stopped or terminated by an alarm action, while instances with the instance store as the root device can only be terminated.
q: Can an alarm stop an EC2 instance whose root device is the instance store?
v: Amazon Elastic Block Store volume as the root device can be stopped or terminated
instance store as the root device can only be terminated
sc: alarms with EC2 stop or terminate actions
ev: Amazon EC2 instances that use an Amazon Elastic Block Store volume as the root device can be stopped or terminated, whereas instances that use the instance store as the root device can only be terminated.

claim: To set up a CloudWatch alarm action that can reboot, stop or terminate an instance, you must use the service-linked IAM role AWSServiceRoleForCloudWatchEvents.
q: Which IAM role do CloudWatch alarm actions that reboot, stop or terminate an instance use?
sc: alarms with EC2 reboot, stop or terminate actions
ev: To set up a CloudWatch alarm action that can reboot, stop, or terminate an instance, you must use a service-linked IAM role, *AWSServiceRoleForCloudWatchEvents*.

claim: A composite alarm determines its state by monitoring the states of other alarms; you define rules that combine those states using Boolean logic.
q: What does a composite alarm monitor, and how do you combine its inputs?
v: determine their state by monitoring the states of other alarms
ev: Composite alarms are alarms that determine their state by monitoring the states of other alarms. You define rules to combine the status of those monitored alarms using Boolean logic.

claim: You can use composite alarms to reduce alarm noise by taking actions only at an aggregated level; once the composite alarm has notified a team, further related alarms do not send new notifications.
q: How can you reduce alarm noise with CloudWatch?
ev: You can use composite alarms to reduce alarm noise by taking actions only at an aggregated level.

If other alarms related to your web server also go into the ALARM state, your team does not get overloaded with new notifications since the composite alarm has already notified them about the existing situation.

claim: Composite alarms can send SNS notifications when they change state and can create investigations, Systems Manager OpsItems or incidents when they go into ALARM state, but they cannot perform EC2 actions or Auto Scaling actions.
q: Can a composite alarm stop an EC2 instance or scale an Auto Scaling group?
v: can't perform EC2 actions or Auto Scaling actions
send Amazon SNS notifications when they change state
n: The composite alarms page (alarm-combining) lists SNS, Lambda, OpsItems and incidents; the alarms overview page lists SNS, investigations, OpsItems and incidents. Both agree that EC2 and Auto Scaling actions are not possible.
ev: Composite alarms can send Amazon SNS notifications when they change state, and can create investigations, Systems Manager OpsItems, or incidents when they go into ALARM state, but can't perform EC2 actions or Auto Scaling actions.

claim: All underlying alarms of a composite alarm must be in the same account and Region as the composite alarm, except in a CloudWatch cross-account observability monitoring account, where the underlying alarms can watch metrics in different source accounts.
q: Can a composite alarm combine alarms from other accounts or Regions?
v: same account and the same Region
ev: All the underlying alarms in your composite alarm must be in the same account and the same Region as your composite alarm. However, if you set up a composite alarm in a CloudWatch cross-account observability monitoring account, the underlying alarms can watch metrics in different source accounts and in the monitoring account itself.

claim: Composite alarm rule expressions combine alarm states with the logical operators AND, OR and NOT.
q: Which operators can a composite alarm rule use?
ev: | AND | Logical AND operator. Returns TRUE when all specified conditions are TRUE. |
| OR | Logical OR operator. Returns TRUE when at least one of the specified conditions is TRUE. |
| NOT | Logical NOT operator. Returns TRUE when the specified condition is FALSE. |

claim: Alarm Mute Rules automatically mute alarm actions during predefined time windows, while CloudWatch continues to monitor and evaluate the alarm states.
q: How can you stop alarm notifications during planned maintenance without disabling the alarms?
v: mute alarm actions during predefined time windows
continue monitoring and evaluating alarm states
ev: Alarm Mute Rules is a CloudWatch feature that provides you a mechanism to automatically mute alarm actions during predefined time windows.
CloudWatch will continue monitoring and evaluating alarm states while preventing unwanted notifications or automated alarm actions during expected operational events.

claim: Alarm mute rules temporarily mute actions during scheduled time windows and unmute automatically when the window ends, whereas the DisableAlarmActions API disables alarm actions until you manually call EnableAlarmActions.
q: What is the difference between an alarm mute rule and DisableAlarmActions?
v: automatically unmute when the window ends
ev: Alarm mute rules temporarily mute actions during scheduled time windows and automatically unmute when the window ends. In contrast, the `DisableAlarmActions` API permanently disables alarm actions until you manually call `EnableAlarmActions`.

claim: Muting an alarm does not stop CloudWatch from sending alarm events for alarm create, update, delete and state changes to Amazon EventBridge.
q: Does muting an alarm stop its events to EventBridge?
v: does not stop CloudWatch from sending alarm events
ev: Muting an alarm does not stop CloudWatch from sending alarm events for alarm create, update, delete, and state changes to Amazon EventBridge.
